facts.claim: How many times an hour a serac, or ice from the West Shoulder, falls on a climber under it, in the cold of the night and in clear weather. Fitted so that crossing the Icefall quickly, before dawn, is the safe way: the time spent under the seracs is what counts.

How many times its rate at night falling ice is at the warmest hour of a clear day. Fitted so that a climber who lingers under the seracs in the afternoon sun is caught several times as often as one who crosses before dawn: the sources name the afternoon the Icefall's worst time.
How many times its rate falling ice is while snow falls: the same, since seracs fall as the glacier moves and the sun warms them.
How many times its rate falling ice is in a strong wind: the same.

How many seconds pass between the crack of a serac breaking and its ice coming down on the climbers below. Seracs fall with little warning, so this is only the crack and the moment the ice takes to fall: someone at the edge may get clear, few others.
The chance falling ice kills outright a climber it catches who isn't clipped to a rope. Fitted to the Icefall's collapses, which killed most of those under the ice.
The chance falling ice kills outright a climber it catches who is clipped to a rope: a little less, since the rope holds them in the fall but not under the ice.

How many times an hour an avalanche comes down on a climber under its slope, in the cold of the night and in clear weather. Fitted so that it's rarer than falling ice in clear weather, and that the time spent under the slope is what counts.
How many times its rate at night an avalanche is at the warmest hour of a clear day, as the sun warms the snow.
How many times its rate an avalanche is while snow falls. Fitted so that a slope loaded with fresh snow is the worst place to be, and waiting out a storm in camp the right call.
How many times its rate an avalanche is in a strong wind, which drifts snow onto the slopes below the ridges.

How many seconds a serac's ice takes to fall to the route once it breaks off (#229), life size, as the game's falls are: a body falls the 15 to 21 m the picture draws the seracs over the route, over the 9 m the sources give the Icefall's own, in about 2 s. It comes after the crack (hazards.serac-warning), so the ice comes down as fast as ice does: whoever is at the edge of the stretch can get clear, few others.

How many seconds pass between the roar of an avalanche starting above and its reaching the climbers below. Fitted so that a climber near the edge of its path can get out of it, and one in the middle rarely can.
The chance an avalanche kills outright a climber it catches who isn't clipped to a rope, buried or swept away: a big one leaves no chance.
The chance an avalanche kills outright a climber it catches who is clipped to a rope: the rope keeps them from being swept away, not from burial.

How many times an hour a snow bridge over a hidden crevasse gives way under a climber on it, in the cold of the night and in clear weather. Fitted so that the time spent on the bridges is what counts.
How many times its rate at night a snow bridge gives way at the warmest hour of a clear day: the bridges hold best in the cold and soften in the sun, which the Western Cwm's heat makes worst.
How many times its rate a snow bridge gives way while snow falls, which hides the crevasses under thinner bridges.
How many times its rate a snow bridge gives way in a strong wind: the same.
How many seconds of warning a snow bridge gives before it gives way: none, which is why the rope matters.
The chance a climber who isn't clipped to a rope dies when a snow bridge gives way under them, falling into the crevasse.
The chance a climber clipped to a rope dies when a snow bridge gives way under them: none, since the rope holds them, as it would have held the Sherpa who fell from a ladder in 2012.

How many times an hour a cornice on the summit ridge breaks under a climber on it, in the cold of the night and in clear weather. Fitted so that a break is rare, and the time spent on the corniced ridge, in a queue above all, is what counts.
How many times its rate at night a cornice breaks at the warmest hour of a clear day, as the sun softens it.
How many times its rate a cornice breaks while snow falls, which builds it out and loads it.
How many times its rate a cornice breaks in a strong wind, which builds cornices out over the Kangshung Face.
How many seconds of warning a cornice gives before it breaks: none, as on the Hillary Step in 2024, where the fixed rope held those who were clipped.
The chance a climber who isn't clipped to a rope dies when a cornice breaks under them, a fall down the Kangshung Face.
The chance a climber clipped to the fixed rope dies when a cornice breaks under them. Fitted to the 2024 collapse, where the rope held several of those who fell.
The hour of the day the sun starts to warm the ice, from which the hazards rise with the day's warmth. Fitted to the sources' advice to be through the Icefall early, before the sun warms the glacier.
The hour the day is warmest, when the hazards are likeliest: the afternoon sun on the seracs.
The hour the day's warmth is over, and the ice is as stable as in the night again.
How much of the sun's warmth reaches the ice under cloud, as a share of a clear day's.
How much of the sun's warmth reaches the ice while snow falls, as a share of a clear day's: none.

How many of the mountain's seconds a serac collapse staged for training cracks and groans before it comes down (#209), as a flight simulator stages an engine failure: long enough for a player who reads the crack to stop or back off, under two seconds of play at the mountain's pace (time.compression), where a real serac gives little warning (hazards.serac-warning).

How far short of the stretch a staged serac collapse comes down on the first climber has to be to set it cracking (#209): close enough that one who walks on into the crack is under it as it falls, and far enough that one who stops at once is spared.
How long a stretch of the route a staged serac collapse buries in blocks of ice (#209): a serac's fall across the route, a few of the Icefall's towers wide (route.icefall-hazards).
The shortest crossing a ladder staged to break for training is laid across (#209): a long crossing, where a fall into the crevasse is the rope's to hold (route.icefall-ladders-lashed).

facts.question: How often do seracs fall, avalanches come down, snow bridges give way and cornices break on a climber under them, and how much likelier is each in the afternoon sun than before dawn? The game uses rates fitted to the advice to cross early and fast; no source read gives a number.
How much do falling snow, cloud and a strong wind change each hazard? After how much fresh snow is an avalanche slope to be avoided, and for how long after it falls?

What happens to a climber caught by falling ice, an avalanche, or a breaking snow bridge or cornice, while clipped to the fixed rope? Does the rope hold them, as it held several climbers in the 2024 cornice collapse, and how badly are they hurt? How many of those caught die, on a rope and off it? How much warning does each give, and what should a climber do with it? The game spares whoever got clear in the warning, kills some of those caught at each kind's odds, and knocks the rest off their feet at 3 m/s down the slope, held by their rope if they're clipped.

facts.claim: How many times an hour a gust comes across the Icefall's open ground with a climber on it, in the cold of the night and in clear weather (#197). Fitted so that a crossing before dawn meets one now and then, from time to time as the sources have it, and the morning's several.
How many times its rate at night a gust comes at the warmest hour of a clear day: the sun's thermals bring the cross wind.
How many times its rate a gust comes while snow falls: a storm's wind.
How many times its rate a gust comes in a strong wind.

How many of the mountain's seconds a gust shows coming, the snow streaming across the slope and its roar, before it hits (#197): long enough for a player who sees it to stop and brace, a second of play at the mountain's pace (time.compression), where a real gust gives a few seconds' warning.

The chance a gust slips a climber on the move on a ladder, blue ice, the front points or steep snow, at a steady pace's sure-footedness (#197); a careful one, braced, far less. Fitted so that an unclipped climber caught on a ladder by a gust risks a fall, and a clipped one only hangs.

How many times an hour a lashed ladder twists at its lashings under a climber on it, in the cold of the night and in clear weather (#197). Fitted so that a crossing of the Icefall's long ladders meets one now and then.
How many times its rate at night a lashed ladder twists at the warmest hour of a clear day: the sun softens the ice its anchors are in.
How many times its rate a lashed ladder twists while snow falls: the same.
How many times its rate a lashed ladder twists in a strong wind, which sways it.

How many of the mountain's seconds a lashed ladder creaks and starts to sway before it twists under the climber on it (#197): long enough to stop and hold the rope, under a second of play at the mountain's pace (time.compression).

The chance a ladder's twist slips a climber on the move on it, at a steady pace's sure-footedness (#197); a careful one, braced, far less. Fitted so that the twist is a scare more often than a slip, which the rope holds.
